Subject: Marketplace: clarifying where customer data lives and how deletion is executed

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks for the walkthrough on Monday — helpful. Before I share the listing internally I need a succinct answer for our engineering and legal teams: when a customer on TerraFin subscribes via the marketplace, what are the guarantees around (1) where inference request data is hosted by region (AWS/GCP/Azure), (2) how long logs/tx traces are retained by default vs. what we can commit for the marketplace listing, and (3) the mechanics for deletion on demand (e.g., do you purge KV-caches, audit logs, backups in all stages?).

We have three specific asks:
- A short table mapping: customer region -> default cloud region used (and fallback behavior).
- Retention defaults for request logs, audit logs, and model cache (with config knobs we can set in Marketplace listing).
- Step-by-step for a deletion request (who is notified, expected SLA, confirm whether backups are affected).

If you can attach a single-page summary + any diagrams, that would be great — TerraFin wants to include this in their vendor risk review on Friday.

Best,

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a compact pack that should map to the three asks. High level answers below and the attachments contain the granular notes/schemas: Residency_SLA_table.xlsx (mapping + defaults) and DataFlow_Diagram_v2.png (flow for requests, KV cache, backups).

High level:
- Region mapping: by default we route inference traffic to the customer-facing region you select in the marketplace listing. For customers in NA we use our us-west-2 (AWS) or us-central (GCP) endpoints depending on availability and the listing config; we can pin listings to a single cloud region on request. Fallback: policy-based routing to nearest supported region; fallbacks are logged and surfaced to the account team.

- Retention defaults (configurable per-listing):
  - Request logs: 30 days (default), configurable to 90/365 on paid tiers; can be shortened to 7 days for compliance-sensitive listings.
  - Audit logs (access control, admin events): 365 days by default (SLA customers can request longer retention).
  - Model KV cache: ephemeral by design; KV cache persists for active sessions and is expired after 24 hours of inactivity by default. We do not persist full trace dumps unless explicitly enabled.

- Deletion flow (summary):
  1) Customer or TerraFin requests deletion via console/API or via support ticket.
  2) Request is triaged by our ops automation; sensitive requests create an audit record and trigger deletion in serving runtime.
  3) We delete request logs, purge KV entries, and mark associated artifacts for removal from backups.
  4) Backups: snapshots are not immediately destroyed; they are marked and included in the next lifecycle prune (we can expedite for marketplace partners with an agreed SLA).
  5) Confirmation: we send a deletion confirmation to the requester and CC the account owner and TerraFin legal if requested.

I'll attach the table and diagram; Ben — adding you here in case TerraFin's procurement wants a standard SLA clause inserted in the MOA.

Thanks,

Hi — quick answers and proposed text you can drop into the questionnaire / MOA: 

1) Deletion certificate: yes — our ops automation produces a signed deletion certificate (SHA256 fingerprint of deleted artifact list + timestamp + operator id). We can attach the certificate to the ticket and provide a signed PDF within 24 hours of completion for marketplace customers.

Proposed MOA language (suggested):
"Redwood will execute deletion requests initiated by the reseller or subscriber and provide a deletion certificate that enumerates removed artifacts and timestamps. Deletion of logs and ephemeral caches will be completed within the agreed SLA; snapshots and backups will be marked for immediate removal and purged per agreed backup lifecycle timelines unless expedited removal is requested under the partner SLA."

2) Cross-cloud backups: treated the same — Redwood's backup lifecycle manager tracks replication targets. For marketplace listings that pin to a single cloud we will include an explicit statement that backups replicated for DR across other clouds will be included in deletion workflows. If TerraFin requires mandatory cross-cloud purge within a specific timeframe (e.g., 48–72 hours), we should document that as an SLA item in the MOA.

Next steps:
- I attached a one-page table and the diagram in my first reply; I'll also upload the Residency_SLA_table.xlsx to the shared Drive link and drop a draft MOA with the suggested clause for your redlines.
- Ben: can you confirm commercial terms for the 48–72 hour expedited purge add-on so I can include it in the MOA?

Thanks,
Olga
